page: Microsoft Azure F16als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Falsv7 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, resulting in a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core performance is more varied; Geekbench multi-core scores rank in the top tier, while stress-ng multi-core performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average category. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks consistently register in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the F16als_v7 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2:1 and the complete absence of local storage. This makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data caching. However, its high clock speed and strong single-threaded performance make it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as single-threaded data processing, image processing, text processing, lightweight software compilation, and small-scale LLM inference, where it demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds for 135M parameter models.
